summary:
We have created an interactive neuroscience-based game called the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. This uses real NASA data and space exploration to create an educational 3d game. It contains interconnected missions which allow young people to experience what it would be like to become an astronaut. The missions include exploring mars, creating habitats, investigating storms and managing resources. 
 
We have used Series Game Mechanics (SGM) and Neuroscience-Informed SGM (NI-SGM). We have used increasing challenges, interactive simulations, mini games and data dashboards to create an active way to learn, think critically and make decisions. 
 
This project solves the problem by making space science more accessible, engaging and practical for younger generations. The young people can explore real mission situations, analyse data from NASA, interpret scientific evidence and make decisions. 
 
This project is important as it helps to connect real life STEM education with space exploration. This inspires the next generation of scientists, engineers and astrnauts.
details:
The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational mission based game which introduces children to space exploration.

This project simplifies complex space science topics and turns them into a mission driven game. Children will become junior astronauts who will go through various scenarios such as exploring Mars, investigating storms, creating habitats and managing resources. Alongside this, they will discover scientific data, analyse images and environmental data, solve problems and make decisions based on the information available.

We have used Series Game Mechanics (SGM) and Neuroscience-Informed Series Game Mechanics (NI-SGM). SGM helps to structure the missions into a learning journey. NI-SGM uses learning theories such as engagement, concentration, feedback and retention.

This project will help to improve scientific knowledge, critical thinking, problem solving, decision making and increase interest in STEM. This will make space science more accessible to children and encourage them to pursue a career in science.

Our project is creative as it uses real NASA resources to create an educational game. We encourage children to engage with the information and use it to solve problems within the missions.

When designing our project we considered the age and level of education of the children. We also considered how easy it would be to access, how scientific it was, how engaging it would be, how challenging the missions would be and how it links to real NASA data.

This project uses NASA resources, scientific data, images and mission information. This can be created using programming and interactive tools to create an engaging

learning environment.
